A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-theoretic evaluation study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated and removed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across translation, summarization, and peer review, including discrimination results and adversarial transformations in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds item-level AUC evaluation, model ablations, and additional case-study results in Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: The operative pairwise information-scoring approach is retained: v1 Figure 1 already shows a binary critic evaluating real and shuffled pairs. V3 formalizes the variational score and overseer incentives, while retaining the earlier three-level appendix prompt. These changes do not establish a different implemented algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use two German–English translation datasets, seven summarization datasets, and ICLR 2023 peer review, with the same strategy families and four tampering scenarios. V3's discussion of expanding from three to ten domains concerns preregistration history; v1 already evaluated all ten.

E2.justification: V3 adds a text-embedding-3-large cosine-similarity baseline in the Opus Books and PubMed model ablation. It also reports both judge baselines for WMT14 in Table 2, where v1 had no judge results. The principal comparator set otherwise remains.

E3.justification: V3 adds per-source AUC evaluation distinguishing Faithful–Faithful from Faithful–Problematic pairs, with symmetric information scores, judge win-rate aggregation, and macro-averaging. It introduces Llama-3.3-70B ablations on Opus Books (n=30) and PubMed (n=100), and changes tampering reporting from percentages to raw score changes and absolute changes in Cohen's d.

E4.justification: V3 adds an item-level validity check asking whether large aggregate effect sizes translate into discrimination within individual sources, alongside a model-sensitivity ablation and an expanded ICLR inversion case study. Existing compression, information-structure, verbosity, and four-transformation analyses are retained; their relocation alone is not an addition.

E5.justification: V3 retains bootstrap confidence intervals but adds a separate 10,000-iteration item-resampling procedure for AUC, whereas v1 specifies 1,000 comparison-level resamples for effect sizes. Table 2 newly states multiple-testing adjustment, and Table 5 adds confidence intervals for tampering score changes. These do not establish additional independent model runs.

E6.justification: Existing means change: Opus Books TVD-MI d changes from 1.97 to 3.08, and the no-reference judge changes from 0.28 to -0.62 in Table 2. V3 adds substantial AUC, ablation, and ICLR case-study results, including TVD-MI AUC 0.544 for peer review and 0.707–0.759 under Reddit TIFU attacks. These are revised or newly reported findings, not uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 removes v1's uniqueness theorem, replaces the empirical frequency-type definition with an empirical joint type, and formalizes signal-only post-processing restrictions. It revises the divergence-generator conditions and kappa relationship and adds variational and reliability derivations. The original sample-complexity bound is retained as Theorem 3.3, but v1's detailed appendix proof is removed, leaving a revised main-text sketch and an appendix restatement.

C1.justification: V3 drops the headline uniqueness claim and the claimed 10–100× robustness advantage. It foregrounds distribution-free certification, black-box TVD-MI, and a new contribution concerning item-level detection without references, supported by AUC results. The compression optimum is no longer a central advertised contribution.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly recognizes that adaptive shared-overlap attacks can increase agreement while reducing usefulness, and that bounded scores do not ensure robust rankings. It distinguishes information preservation from correctness, discourages standalone quality ranking, and treats the inverted-U pattern as model- and dataset-specific behavior rather than a resolution of worst-case theoretical limits.

D1.justification: The new methodology appendix substantially expands reproducibility information: evaluation temperature, translation token limits, AUC aggregation, judge prompts, overall computation and cost, and preregistration deviations. Section 4.2.1 specifies the case-flipping, hashing, and padding operations. Existing generation configurations and the code-access link are retained; much of this is fuller disclosure rather than evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning around GEM, contrastive learning, RLHF/Constitutional AI, and additional divergence, concentration, and reliability literature, while removing TwS and several earlier references. Table 1 shifts the comparison toward reference-free operation, distribution-free analysis, and black-box access, replacing the earlier emphasis on equilibrium and strategy-proofness guarantees.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical framework, research questions, and discussion are substantially rewritten and reorganized. V3 adds an extended methodology appendix and moves the compression and judge-inversion discussions into Appendix B. The title also changes from LLM-Based to AI-Based Evaluation.

P2.justification: V3 changes the publication layout, adds model-ablation and AUC tables, transposes the tampering table, and expands the case-study table to two domains. Figure 1 revises rate labels and corrects its illustrated TVD-MI score from 1.33 to 0.33. The unchanged compression plot moves to the appendix rather than becoming a new figure.

improvement.justification: The item-level AUC validation, model check, and explicit applicability limits make the empirical conclusions more defensible than reliance on aggregate effect sizes alone. Expanded protocol and preregistration disclosures also improve auditability. These gains are tempered by removal of the detailed bound proof and new reporting inconsistencies: for example, v3 Section 5.1 claims six successful no-reference judge domains, while Table 2 reports four. The net improvement is therefore limited.
